name: espresso
description: View and change Espresso AI optimization settings for your Snowflake and Databricks accounts.

interface.longDescription: Espresso AI cuts Snowflake and Databricks compute costs. Connect your Espresso account to check which warehouses the Warehouse Agent and Scheduler manage, review recent settings changes, and turn optimizations on or off for specific warehouses, Snowflake query routing, and Databricks Spark jobs.
defaultPrompt: Which of my Snowflake warehouses does Espresso manage?
What changed in my Espresso settings this week?
Add a warehouse to the Espresso Scheduler.

positive.description: List the Espresso accounts the user can manage
positive.prompt: Which Espresso accounts can I manage?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists one account, MCP Demo Account (mcp_demo_account), as a Snowflake account. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: Review Warehouse Agent settings and cluster limits
positive.prompt: Which of my Snowflake warehouses does Espresso manage, and what are their cluster limits?
positive.expected_behavior: Says the Warehouse Agent is off and Espresso manages none of the five warehouses yet. Lists DEMO_WH_1 to DEMO_WH_5 with their sizes (X-Small to X-Large) and min/max clusters (1-2, 1-3, 1-4, 2-6, 1-8). Nothing is changed.

positive.description: Turn on the Warehouse Agent with a preview and confirmation
positive.prompt: Turn on the Espresso Warehouse Agent for my account.
positive.expected_behavior: Previews the Warehouse Agent going from off to on and asks for confirmation. After the user confirms, applies the change and confirms the agent is on.

positive.description: Enable one warehouse and raise its cluster limit
positive.prompt: Enable Espresso on DEMO_WH_3 and raise its max clusters to 6.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows a diff for DEMO_WH_3 only: enabled goes from false to true and max clusters from 4 to 6. Applies after the user confirms. The other warehouses don't change.

positive.prompt: Is the Espresso Scheduler on, and how is each warehouse set up for scheduling?
positive.expected_behavior: Says the Scheduler is off and lists the five warehouses with scheduling off, no routing pool and 0 max extra warehouses. Notes there are no routing pools. Nothing is changed.

negative.description: The Scheduler can't be turned on while the Warehouse Agent is off. The assistant should explain that and offer to turn the Warehouse Agent on first, changing nothing.
ANALYTICS_WH doesn't exist in the account. The assistant should say so, list DEMO_WH_1 to DEMO_WH_5 and ask which warehouse was meant, changing nothing.
negative.prompt: Set max clusters to 10 on ANALYTICS_WH.

negative.description: Deleting Snowflake warehouses is outside the plugin's scope. The assistant should say it can't delete warehouses through Espresso and that no change was made.
negative.prompt: Delete DEMO_WH_2 from my Snowflake account.
